# cronli5

> Turns cron patterns into plain-language descriptions ("every 15 minutes
> from 9 a.m. through 5:45 p.m. on weekdays") in eleven languages: English,
> Czech, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese, Russian,
> Ukrainian and Chinese (Simplified). Zero runtime dependencies, ESM and CommonJS,
> TypeScript types bundled, Node 20+ or the browser. It describes
> schedules; it does not run them or compute next run times.

Install: `npm install cronli5`

## API

```js
import cronli5 from 'cronli5';

cronli5('*/5 * * * *');                     // 'every 5 minutes'
cronli5('30 9 * * 1-5');                    // 'at 9:30 a.m. on weekdays'
cronli5('0 0 * * *', { form: 'label' });    // 'At midnight every day'
cronli5('0 0 * * *', { form: 'sentence' }); // 'Runs at midnight every day.'
cronli5({ hour: 9, minute: 30 });           // 'at 9:30 a.m. every day'
```

The pattern is a string, an array of fields, or an object of named fields.
Five fields are standard cron; six put seconds first; seven add a year
last. `@daily` and the other aliases, wrap-around ranges (`22-2`) and the
Quartz tokens `L`, `W` and `#` are accepted.

Other languages are separate modules, so only what you import is bundled:

```js
import cronli5 from 'cronli5';
import de from 'cronli5/lang/de';

cronli5('30 9 * * 1-5', { lang: de });      // 'montags bis freitags um 9:30 Uhr'
```

`import cronli5 from 'cronli5/all'` knows every language by code
(`{ lang: 'de' }`). `create({ languages: [de, ja] })` makes an instance
that knows the languages you choose.

Options (second argument): `lang` (code such as `'en-GB'`, or an imported
module), `form` (`'fragment'` default, `'label'`, `'sentence'`), `style`
(the language's style table, e.g. `{ hour12: false }` in English), `cron`
(`'standard'` or `'quartz'`, which numbers weekdays from 1 = Sunday and
accepts `?`), `seconds`, `years`, and `lenient` (return a fallback text
instead of throwing on a bad pattern). A bad pattern throws
`Cronli5InputError`; an option it cannot honour throws
`Cronli5OptionError`, even when lenient.

Command line: `npx cronli5 '*/15 9-17 * * 1-5'`, or
`crontab -l | npx cronli5 --crontab`.

## Coming from cRonstrue

`cronli5/compat` takes the same `toString(pattern, options)` call as
cRonstrue. Each cRonstrue option is mapped or refused with an error.

```js
import cronli5 from 'cronli5/compat';

cronli5.toString('30 9 * * 1-5'); // 'At 09:30 AM Monday through Friday'
```

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/andrewbroz/cronli5#readme): usage, options, languages, examples
- [Migrating from cRonstrue](https://github.com/andrewbroz/cronli5/blob/main/docs/migrating-from-cronstrue.md): option mapping and output differences
- [cronli5 vs. cRonstrue](https://github.com/andrewbroz/cronli5/blob/main/docs/cronli5-vs-cronstrue.md): generated side-by-side output
- [Style tables](https://github.com/andrewbroz/cronli5/blob/main/docs/styles.md): every style field per language
- [Per-language docs](https://github.com/andrewbroz/cronli5/tree/main/docs/lang): each language's conventions

## Optional

- [Conformance suites](https://github.com/andrewbroz/cronli5/tree/main/conformance): every expected description per language as JSON, for ports to other programming languages
- [Design](https://github.com/andrewbroz/cronli5/blob/main/docs/i18n-design.md): core and per-language renderers
